cases.title: Read-only database diagnostics
cases.surface: `newheap-db` direct schema and JSON query contracts plus consumer-owned governed schema, indexes and query MCP tools
cases.outcome: Developers and agents take the repository-declared database fast path without inspecting application code, settings, secrets or package internals to rediscover routing or JSON fields: one bounded tracked-file search finds a nested catalog, its directory becomes the diagnostic working directory, and its only profile automatically selects the provider, configuration path, connection-string name, ceilings and default environment. Local `validate` opens no connection and advertises the `outbound-network` capability required by `schema` and `query`; Codex starts those execution commands with a narrow reusable `newheap-db` network permission instead of first probing its restricted sandbox. When the user explicitly requests another runtime environment, `--environment` applies it consistently to schema and query without requiring a duplicate profile solely for Production or Staging; the governed connection-string name and read-only-principal verification remain unchanged. `newheap-db` resolves that name through the selected environment's normal configuration and secrets flow without exposing the connection string. A direct `schema --search ... --describe-if-single` invocation needs no JSON schema request and returns a unique match plus its exact columns, indexes and relationships through one connection and read-only transaction; zero or multiple matches remain bounded summaries. `schema` and `query` validate internally, so interactive diagnostics do not spend a separate call on `validate`. The executable sample prompt uses Production from a Development-default profile, counts projects and returns the latest by `CreationDateTime` with exactly one schema invocation and one query invocation. Checked-in schema and query requests remain repeatable CI and dry-run contracts. Permission-filtered exact descriptions expose named outgoing and incoming relationships with ordered column pairs and validation status, while at most one focused index lookup may inform an immediately useful predicate or ordering. Structured MCP input and the direct CLI `--request-file` option keep serialized JSON out of Windows process arguments. The executable sample MCP fixes profile, capability, a sixteen-call budget and ceilings server-side, requires an explicit requested row count, rejects excessive requests before execution, and fails without partial data when actual results exceed the accepted limit, while SQL Server and PostgreSQL enforce dedicated read-only credentials and return only safe provider classifications, codes, stages and retry hints. Unknown connection failures become transient `connection-failed` outcomes without weakening `authentication-failed` or `database-not-found`, and no server name, credential or provider exception text reaches the response. An unresolved NewHeap secret returns `connection-string-unresolved` with the process-local secrets-path remediation, while malformed resolved provider configuration returns `connection-configuration-invalid`; neither exposes its value or produces schema or query evidence. A checked-in exact local path may be applied to the `newheap-db` child process for one schema retry without permanently changing Production settings. Every other non-success governed schema response ends the diagnostic attempt, so agents do not infer deployed identifiers, relationships, enum values or business semantics from source code or a repository index and do not issue a data query.

cases.outcome: An agent can change one project status only inside its authorized division and narrow manage capability after exact proposal approval and mandatory budget reservation; the same idempotency key cannot repeat or alter the side effect, and success is reported only after an independent status read verifies the result.

cases.title: Policy-bound Agent Framework adapter
cases.surface: `NhAiAgentDescriptor`, `INhAiAgentFrameworkAdapter`, Microsoft Agent Framework `ChatClientAgent`, named model profiles, and generated Agent-exposed tools
cases.outcome: A stable non-human project agent returns structured creation outcomes, resolves its consumer-owned model profile and receives only attested actor-specific tools inside its allow-list and autonomy ceiling; every model call crosses shared classification, budget, deadline, usage and telemetry governance.

cases.title: Authorized hierarchical AI context
cases.surface: `INhAiContextResolver`, authorization-first context sources, execution-scope filtering, provenance, trust classification, conflict resolution, and content budgets
cases.outcome: Project descriptions are retrieved only after source authorization, remain limited to the active division, carry provenance and untrusted-data metadata, and are deterministically deduplicated and budgeted before prompt formatting; instruction-like document text gains no authority.

cases.title: Versioned AI instruction asset
cases.surface: `NhAiTextAssetFactory`, `NhAiAssetManifest`, prompt version/hash binding, required model/tool contracts, context policy, retention, and evaluation baseline metadata
cases.outcome: Project-agent instructions remain normal application-owned text while a content-free manifest records their stable identity, hash, provenance, capabilities, tool contracts, context policy, classification, retention, and evaluation baseline; agent and approval evidence bind the version and hash without logging content.

cases.title: Governed external MCP tool import
cases.surface: `INhAiMcpClientToolImporter`, explicit per-server allow-list and namespace, local effect and authorization metadata, bounded remote schemas and results, and shared invocation governance
cases.outcome: Only the explicitly allowlisted external lookup is imported under a collision-safe namespace; its remote description grants no authority, an unlisted destructive-looking tool remains absent, and bounded arguments still cross NewHeap authorization, capability, budget, timeout, concurrency, idempotency, result-bound, and audit controls.

cases.title: Durable external-signal suspension and wake-up
cases.surface: `INhBackgroundOperationSuspensionContext`, `INhBackgroundOperationSignalService`, `WaitingForSignal`, typed checkpoint signals, durable expiry, duplicate detection, cancellation, and dispatcher wake-up
cases.outcome: A running operation atomically suspends its attempt and releases the worker, accepts one owner-bound typed signal, treats an identical duplicate idempotently, rejects a conflicting signal, resumes as a new fenced attempt, preserves completed idempotent work, and remains cancellable or expiry-wakeable without polling.

cases.title: Approval-gated durable AI portfolio report
cases.surface: `INhAiBackgroundOperationRunAdapter`, non-human run binding, application snapshot, server-created `NhAiProposal`, canonical `INhAiApprovalValidator`, exact approval signal, idempotent artifact publication, and plan/execute/verify progress
cases.outcome: A division-scoped report binds its background-operation ID, attempt, idempotency key and fencing token to a non-human AI invocation, persists application-owned snapshot state plus a server-created canonical proposal and content-free workflow checkpoint, validates the durable approver against that proposal after wake-up, and resumes without conversation history or duplicate publication.

cases.title: Authorized provider-neutral AI ingestion
cases.surface: `INhAiIngestionPipeline`, authorization-before-read, immutable version leases, budgeted named embedding profiles, deterministic chunks, canonical hashes, and the standard Microsoft `VectorStore` abstraction
cases.outcome: A division-scoped document is never opened before read and replacement-delete authorization, remains untrusted data with provenance and classification, and is embedded only after an immutable source/document/version lease plus mandatory model-budget reservation succeed; denial or conflict performs no embedding or vector write.

cases.title: Content-free AI model usage and streaming telemetry
cases.surface: `INhAiChatExecutor`, named profile and run-budget enforcement, OpenTelemetry activities and metrics, `INhAiUsageSink`, token/latency/TTFT accounting, and cancellation-safe streaming
cases.outcome: Model calls and streams preserve standard Microsoft AI responses while recording bounded profile, version, token, size, latency, finish and scope metadata; prompts, responses, model deployment identifiers and provider errors are absent from usage records, cancelled streams propagate cancellation, and dependency failures end in a safe `TaskResult` completion.

cases.title: Versioned AI safety evaluation gate
cases.surface: Microsoft `IEvaluator`, `NhAiEvaluationDataset`, deterministic scope and injection fixtures, fail-closed metric interpretation, content-free reports, and baseline version/hash evidence
cases.outcome: The project agent's prompt-injection and cross-division fixtures run through Microsoft AI Evaluation contracts against a versioned baseline; missing or inconclusive interpretations fail closed, while persisted reports contain hashes and metric outcomes but no prompt, response, reason or diagnostic content.

cases.title: Native AOT generated AI tool catalog smoke
cases.surface: `NewHeap.Platform.AI.AotSmoke`, generated `INhAiToolCatalog`, canonical schema manifest, trimming, and Native AOT publication
cases.outcome: A trimmed Native AOT executable resolves the generated catalog and creates its local Microsoft AI function without runtime reflection discovery, proving descriptors and schema manifests remain rooted.

cases.title: Durable AI ingestion lifecycle
cases.surface: `INhAiBackgroundOperationIngestionAdapter`, content-free checkpoints, deterministic replacement lineage, authorized deletion, and partial-success batch results
cases.outcome: A durable ingestion attempt resumes without reading or embedding the same document twice, replacement deletion is independently authorized before source access, immutable version/hash/key conflicts cannot overwrite vectors, and a failed batch item does not erase successful document evidence.

cases.title: Version-bound Agent Framework workflow checkpoint
cases.surface: Microsoft Agent Framework `CheckpointInfo`, `INhAiAgentFrameworkWorkflowCheckpointAdapter`, session identity, workflow version, state hash, and durable NewHeap checkpoint references
cases.outcome: An official Agent Framework workflow checkpoint retains its opaque session and checkpoint identity in a content-free durable reference; a changed workflow version, checkpoint lineage or state hash cannot be resumed as the same run.
